He played college basketball for the [[Louisiana–Lafayette Ragin' Cajuns men's basketball|Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns]] and represented the United States at the [[Basketball at the 2015 Pan American Games – Men's tournament|2015 Pan American Games]] in [[Toronto]]. ==High school career== Long attended [[Morgan City High School]]. As a senior, he averaged 21.4 points, 15.2 rebounds and 9.1 blocks, helping team to a 26–5 record. He was named district MVP, earned first team all-district honors for two straight year and was the district defensive player of the year as a senior.{{cite web|url=http://www.ragincajuns.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=4962&path=mbball|title=Louisiana-Lafayette bio|work=RaginCajuns.com|access-date=October 29, 2016}} ==College career== Long originally enrolled at [[Mississippi State University]] of the [[Southeastern Conference]], but became immediately unhappy with his choice. After the first semester, and without playing in any games, Long transferred to [[Louisiana–Lafayette Ragin' Cajuns men's basketball|Louisiana–Lafayette]] and received an [[National Collegiate Athletic Association|NCAA]] waiver to allow him to play the following season without sitting out the customary full year.{{cite web|first=Sam|last=Vecenie|title=Shawn Long overcomes hurdles to be Sun Belt's next NBA hopeful|url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/25425630/shawn-long-overcomes-hurdles-to-be-sun-belts-next-nba-hopeful|work=CBSSports.com|date=December 24, 2015|access-date=January 27, 2016}} Long first suited up for the Ragin' Cajuns in the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13 season]], averaging 15.5 points and 10.2 rebounds per game to earn [[Sun Belt Conference]] Freshman of the Year and second-team All-conference honors. Over his next two seasons, Long would again average a [[Double (basketball)|double-double]] and was named first-team All-Sun Belt both years. For his senior season, Long was named the preseason Sun Belt Player of the Year.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Johnson|url=http://theadvocate.com/sports/latestsports/13767639-31/shawn-long-selected-sun-belt|title=Shawn Long selected Sun Belt Conference preseason player of the year; Cajuns picked to win league|work=[[The Advocate (Louisiana)|The Advocate]]|date=October 21, 2015|access-date=January 27, 2016}} On January 23, 2016, in a game against the [[Troy Trojans men's basketball|Troy Trojans]], Long scored his 2,000th point and became the first player in school and conference history to record 2,000 points and 1,000 rebounds for his career. He was also selected for the [[National Association of Basketball Coaches]] (NABC) college All-Star game to be held at the [[2016 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|2016 Final Four]] in [[Houston]].{{cite web|first=Tim|last=Buckley|url=http://www.theadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/ul/2016/01/27/uls-long-reaches-milestones-marlin-deems-amazing/79351792/|title=UL's Long reaches milestones Marlin deems 'amazing'|work=[[The Daily Advertiser (Lafayette)|The Daily Advertiser]]|date=January 27, 2016|access-date=January 27, 2016}} ==Professional career== ===Delaware and Philadelphia (2016–2017)=== After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Long signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] on July 8, 2016.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-announce-samsung-nba-summer-league-roster-signings|title=Sixers Announce Samsung NBA Summer League Roster, Signings|work=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2016|access-date=July 9, 2016}} He was waived by the 76ers on October 24 after appearing in seven preseason games.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-waive-five-players|title=Sixers Waive Five Players|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=October 24, 2016}} Five days later, he was acquired by the [[Delaware Blue Coats|Delaware 87ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]] as an affiliate player of the 76ers.{{cite web|url=http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/3320/|title=SEVENS INVITE 13 PLAYERS TO TRAINING CAMP|work=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2016|access-date=November 1, 2016|archive-date=November 3, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161103234214/http://delaware.dleague.nba.com/news/3320/|url-status=dead}} On January 6, 2017, Long had 45 points and 14 rebounds in a 129–105 win over the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]].{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20170106/ERIDEL/|title=Long, Sevens Cruise Past BayHawks|work=NBA.com|date=January 6, 2017|access-date=January 6, 2017}} He was selected to play in the [[NBA Development League All-Star Game|2017 NBA D-League All-Star Game]]. On March 6, 2017, he was called up by the 76ers, who signed him to a 10-day contract to help the team deal with numerous injuries. Philadelphia had to use an NBA hardship exemption in order to sign him as he made their roster stand at 16, one over the allowed limited of 15.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-call-long-sevens|title=Sixers Call Up Long from Sevens|work=NBA.com|date=March 6, 2017|access-date=March 6, 2017}} He made his NBA debut that night, recording 13 points and seven rebounds in a 112–98 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900329|title=Antetokounmpo, Snell lead Bucks past 76ers, 112-98|work=ESPN.com|date=March 6, 2017|access-date=March 7, 2017}} On March 16, 2017, he signed a partially guaranteed, multiyear deal with the 76ers.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/sixers-sign-shawn-long|title=Sixers Sign Shawn Long|work=NBA.com|date=March 16, 2017|access-date=March 16, 2017}}{{cite web|last=Pompey|first=Keith|url=http://www.philly.com/philly/blogs/sports/sixers/Source-Sixers-expected-to-sign-Shawn-Long-to-multi-year-deal.html|title=Sixers sign Shawn Long to multi-year deal|work=Philly.com|date=March 16, 2017|access-date=March 16, 2017}} Seven days later, in a 117–107 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]], Long had 18 points in just his ninth career game.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900472|title=Career nights for Saric, Long lift 76ers past Bulls, 117-107|work=ESPN.com|date=March 24, 2017|access-date=March 25, 2017}} On June 28, 2017, Long was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for a 2018 second-round pick and cash considerations.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/sixers-acquire-second-round-pick-houston|title=Sixers Acquire Second-Round Pick From Houston|work=NBA.com|date=June 28, 2017|access-date=June 28, 2017}} He was waived by the Rockets on September 26, 2017.{{cite web|author=Houston Rockets|url=https://twitter.com/HoustonRockets/status/912782068949688321|title=Roster Update: The Rockets have waived...|work=Twitter|date=September 26, 2017|access-date=September 26, 2017}} ===China and G League (2017–2018)=== On October 10, 2017, Long signed a two-month contract with the [[Xinjiang Flying Tigers]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].{{cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/asia/china/249444/shawn-long-agreed-to-terms-with-xinjiang-flying-tigers.html|title=Shawn Long agreed to terms with Xinjiang Flying Tigers|work=sportando.basketball|date=October 10, 2017|access-date=September 3, 2018}} He left the team in mid-November after averaging 12.7 points and 6.1 rebounds in seven games.{{cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/asia/china/254220/shawn-long-to-leave-xinjiang.html|title=Shawn Long to leave Xinjiang|work=sportando.basketball|date=November 16, 2017|access-date=September 3, 2018}} On December 18, 2017, Long was acquired by the [[Delaware Blue Coats|Delaware 87ers]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/transactions/league/2018|title=2017-2018 G League Transactions|work=RealGM.com|access-date=September 3, 2018}} ===New Zealand Breakers and Guizhou Guwutang Tea (2018–2019)=== On September 5, 2018, Long signed with the [[New Zealand Breakers]] for the [[2018–19 NBL season]].{{cite web|url=https://www.foxsports.com.au/basketball/nbl/former-breakers-import-shawn-long-says-hes-agreed-to-sign-with-melbourne-united/news-story/9facbd8022d9da9f8b4ac33f51d0e889|title=Former Breakers import Shawn Long says he's agreed to sign with Melbourne United|work=FoxSports.com.au|date=April 28, 2019|access-date=April 28, 2019}} On May 2, 2019, Long signed with the [[Guizhou Guwutang Tea White Tigers|Guizhou Guwutang Tea]] of the [[National Basketball League (China)|Chinese NBL]].{{cite web |title=官宣！新疆旧将加盟贵州队 朗曾是周琦火箭队友 |url=https://www.163.com/sports/article/EE675EQR0005877V.html
